source.paraphrase: The request body is caller-controlled input. Copying it whole into a record or a DTO copies fields the caller was never offered, such as role or owner.

invariants.why: A spread or assign of req.body lets the caller set privileged fields that the form never showed, and the write persists them.
invariants.fixHint: Destructure the named fields the handler needs from req.body, or validate the body against a schema and use the parsed output.
invariants.avoid: Object.assign without a spread copies the same fields. A default object merged first does not stop the body from overriding it.

source.locator: A01:2021 Broken access control, open redirect
source.paraphrase: The query string and route params are caller-controlled. Sending the client to a URL taken from them lets an attacker bounce victims through your domain to a lookalike.

invariants.why: An open redirect turns the app's domain into a launchpad for phishing: the link looks internal until the browser lands elsewhere.
invariants.fixHint: Redirect to a fixed path, or check the value against an allowlist of destinations before using it.
invariants.avoid: A template literal around the query value is still the query value. Encoding it does not make it a destination you chose.

source.paraphrase: status only sets the code. The request stays open until something sends the body, so a bare status call leaves the client hanging.

invariants.why: A handler that sets a status and never sends holds the connection until the client times out, and the caller cannot tell an error from a slow success.
invariants.fixHint: Chain a sender: res.status(201).json(order), .send, .end, or use res.sendStatus where no body is needed.
invariants.avoid: Referencing .send without calling it sends nothing. Assigning res.statusCode directly has the same hang without a later send.

source.paraphrase: Passing the string route or router to next skips the remaining stack by name. A typo in that string silently changes which handlers run.

invariants.why: String-skipping hides control flow in a magic value: readers cannot see which handlers are bypassed, and a misspelling changes routing without an error.
invariants.fixHint: Call next() to continue or next(err) to fail. If a route must be skipped, restructure the middleware order instead.
invariants.avoid: Quote style does not matter: next('route') skips exactly like next("route"). Passing an error object is the legitimate sibling and stays allowed. The finding is the next call itself, not a call that contains it. The callee must be named next; a callback under another name is not matched.

source.paraphrase: A wildcard allow-origin header tells browsers every site may read the response. With credentials it hands the user's session to any origin that asks.

invariants.why: Manual wildcard headers bypass the cors middleware's origin list and expose authenticated responses to any site the user visits.
invariants.fixHint: Serve CORS through the cors middleware with an explicit origin list, or set the header to the one origin the client runs on.
invariants.avoid: Lowercasing the header name changes nothing on the wire. Using res.header instead of res.set is the same policy.

source.paraphrase: res.sendFile reads the running file system. If the path contains user input, either build it securely or set the root option so Express keeps the resolved path inside that directory.

invariants.why: A route parameter such as ..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd decodes to ../ segments, so path.join walks out of the intended folder and the server sends any readable file.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the user-supplied name as the path with { root: dir }, or reduce it to path.basename(name) before joining it to a fixed directory.
invariants.avoid: A variable named rootDir inside path.join is not the root option. res.download has the same file-system reach. A path destructured from req.params into a local name first is not seen.

source.paraphrase: Express 5 removed app.del, req.param(name), res.sendfile, the res.json(obj, status), res.send(body, status), res.send(status) and res.redirect(url, status) signatures, the back magic string and the singular req.accepts* names. Express 4 already deprecated them.

invariants.why: On Express 5 these calls throw, send the status number as the body, or redirect to a literal /back path. On Express 4 they log deprecation warnings.
invariants.fixHint: Use app.delete, req.params/req.body/req.query, res.sendFile, res.sendStatus(code), res.status(code).json(body), res.redirect(status, url), req.get('Referrer') || '/' and req.acceptsLanguages.
invariants.avoid: res.send('200') with a quoted number is a valid body. res.redirect(301, url) puts the status first and is allowed. del on a cache or Redis client is not an Express router.

source.paraphrase: Cookies carrying session or identity state should set httpOnly and secure so client-side scripts cannot read them and plaintext connections cannot transmit them.

invariants.why: Explicitly setting httpOnly: false exposes cookies to document.cookie theft during XSS, and secure: false allows transmission over unencrypted HTTP.
invariants.fixHint: Set { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' } on res.cookie, or omit explicit false overrides.
invariants.avoid: Only inline object literals passed to res.cookie or response.cookie with literal false for httpOnly or secure are matched. Options built in a separate variable are not tracked.

source.work: Express Production Best Practices: Performance and Reliability (expressjs.com)
source.paraphrase: Synchronous functions tie up the single-threaded Node.js execution loop until they return, stalling every concurrent request.

invariants.why: A single readFileSync or writeFileSync inside a route callback blocks the entire Node process for the duration of disk I/O.
invariants.fixHint: Use async fs/promises methods (await readFile, await writeFile) inside an async route handler, or load static files once at module startup.
invariants.avoid: Synchronous calls at module top-level before app.listen are allowed. Sync calls hidden inside a helper function declared outside the app/router call are not followed.
